title: Initial-Slip Dynamics Enables the Quantum Mpemba Effect
authors: M. Crotti, F. Cavaliere, D. Ferraro, G. Benenti, M. Sassetti
abstract: We investigate the quantum Mpemba effect, whereby a system initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than one initially closer to equilibrium, emerging in a quantum harmonic oscillator linearly coupled to a bosonic environment. Starting from factorized thermal states at different temperatures, we derive exact analytical criteria for the occurrence of the quantum Mpemba effect valid also beyond the typically considered weak-coupling and Markovian approximations. Most importantly, we show that the effect is enabled by the initial-slip dynamics generated by the sudden switch-on of the system-bath interaction. Neglecting this contribution completely suppresses the anomalous relaxation, identifying transient system-bath correlations as the key ingredient underlying the quantum Mpemba effect.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes the quantum Mpemba effect in an oscillator coupled to a bath, proving that the effect requires non-Markovian dynamics. The key finding is that the anomalous fast relaxation is entirely enabled by the initial-slip dynamics generated when the system-bath coupling is suddenly switched on.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantum Mpemba effect, which describes the counter-intuitive phenomenon where a system initially further from equilibrium relaxes faster than one initially closer.
main_result: The quantum Mpemba effect is shown to be critically dependent on the initial-slip dynamics generated by the sudden switch-on of the system-bath interaction, as neglecting this term suppresses the anomalous relaxation.
method: The authors derive exact analytical criteria by analyzing the time evolution of the covariance matrix for a quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to a bosonic bath.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum harmonic oscillator linearly coupled to a bosonic environment (Caldeira–Leggett model). The analysis uses factorized thermal initial states and examines dynamics across various coupling regimes.
key_observables: The diagnostic measure is the Frobenius distance, $D_\alpha(t)$, and the sign change of $\Delta D(t) = D_c(t) - D_h(t)$ indicates the Mpemba effect.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the initial temperatures ($T$ and $T_\alpha$), the coupling strength ($\gamma_0$), and the bath cutoff frequency ($\omega_D$). The analysis focuses on regimes beyond weak-coupling and Markovian approximations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the dynamics remain Gaussian, and the core finding relies on the inclusion of the initial-slip dynamics, which is absent in the Born-Markov approximation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the long-time behavior of the difference function $F(t)$, showing periodic sign changes indicative of the Mpemba effect when initial-slip dynamics are included.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general framework using the covariance matrix, deriving criteria for the effect, and then rigorously demonstrating that the initial-slip contribution is the necessary ingredient for the effect to manifest, contrasting this with the results obtained when this term is neglected.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep, non-trivial understanding of non-equilibrium relaxation dynamics in open quantum systems, showing how transient, non-Markovian correlations (initial-slip) can fundamentally alter macroscopic relaxation behavior.
